newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht surges offshore, interbank rate down.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht surges offshore, interbank rate down.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied against the dollar in offshore markets in late Friday trade as foreign players dumped dollars to raise funds for covering their short baht positions, dealers said.
The baht surged to 24.950/25.050 to the dollar late in offshore markets from 25.250/25.350 in early morning. In domestic market, the baht steadied at about 25.800/25.850 in late trade.
The mid-rate was set at 25.80 per dollar against 25.75 on Thursday.

"The offshore market was quiet but volatile. I heard some investment funds in Hong Kong heavily sold dollar for baht," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "There is nothing exciting in the local market."
Dealers said offshore parties were demanding baht to cover short positions of the currency.

A two-tier offshore and onshore baht market has been in place since mid-May after speculative attacks on the currency which prompted the central bank to impose capital controls to cut off baht supplies for offshore players.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted offshore at 100/140 satangs per dollar and 20/30 satangs locally.
"Swap premiums were shooting up in offshore markets as offshore players tried to roll over forward contracts," said another dealer.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 10.00-12.00 percent late from 12.00-13.00 in early morning, dealers said.
"Interbank rates are expected to firm next week as the government would start drawing corporate tax payment from bank accounts of paying companies," a money market dealer said.
